why: Large Silicon Valley education and youth funder (summer extended learning, Boys & Girls Clubs, YMCA, a school district) through FY2024, but no reading or tutoring grants are evident.
Literacy is its whole focus (84 grants, FY2024): besides adult literacy it funds family literacy, a reading remediation lab, a mobile library and Houston libraries.
Every one of its 16 grants (median $117k, FY2024) funds a literacy-based after-school program for K-3 girls.
Funds a K-3 summer reading initiative plus New Haven Reads and Literacy Volunteers ($85k-$88k each) among 578 Connecticut grants through FY2024.
All 276 grants (through FY2025) provide reading resources to underfunded literacy programs to raise disadvantaged children's reading proficiency.
52 grants through FY2024 donate books for student reading programs at NY schools, a Boys & Girls Club and a summer camp.
Its 452 grants (FY2025) are summer-reading book distributions to Washington elementary schools only, so it supports schools rather than outside tutoring programs.
Funds after-school homework clubs and tutoring, but only inside its own Springfield School District (9 grants, FY2025).
Twelve small grants to Philadelphia schools for varied student programs; only one (an elementary tutoring-and-basketball league) involves tutoring.
Only 3 grants (latest FY2023), for reading programs at Nevada elementary schools; on topic but thin.
